summary: South African trumpeter, flugelhornist and singer who carried township jazz and mbaqanga to international audiences. His 1968 instrumental Grazing in the Grass topped the US pop chart.
know: His first trumpet came from anti-apartheid priest Trevor Huddleston, who later arranged a gift horn from Louis Armstrong for the band Masekela played in.
He played in the Jazz Epistles, the first Black South African jazz group to record an LP.
He played trumpet on The Byrds' So You Want to Be a Rock 'n' Roll Star and appeared at the Monterey Pop Festival in 1967.
keyAlbums: Home Is Where the Music Is

influencedBy.why: Armstrong was his first trumpet hero, and the gifted Armstrong horn tied the two together early.
Gillespie befriended and encouraged him when he arrived in New York and urged him to build on South African sounds.
His early bebop playing and later flugelhorn tone owed a clear debt to Davis.
Makeba, his wife in the mid 1960s and lifelong collaborator, helped him launch his American career.
Time with Fela and the West African scene pushed him toward the Afro-rock and highlife grooves of his Hedzoleh Soundz period.

influenced.why: He played the trumpet part on their 1967 single So You Want to Be a Rock 'n' Roll Star.
When Water charted in the US in 2023, she became the first South African solo act on the Hot 100 since his 1968 run.

cousins.why: Jazz that kept reaching toward funk and wider audiences.
Big, warm horn music built on jazz but aimed at a wide audience.
Jazz-rooted protest music with a deep groove.

summary: Male choral group founded by Joseph Shabalala that made the soft-stepping isicathamiya style famous worldwide. Their work on Paul Simon's Graceland led to a global career and several Grammy Awards.
know: Joseph Shabalala said the group's harmonies came to him in a series of dreams in 1964.
Their 1973 album Amabutho is often cited as the first gold record by Black South African musicians.
Shaka Zulu (1987), produced by Paul Simon, won the Grammy for Best Traditional Folk Recording.
songs: Diamonds on the Soles of Her Shoes

cousins.why: Tight, rhythmic male vocal harmony rooted in sacred music.
Gospel quartet singing where blended voices carry everything.
Polished a cappella quartet work with deep bass and high leads.

summary: Senegalese singer and bandleader who built mbalax, a fusion of sabar drumming, griot singing and Afro-Cuban and pop elements, into one of Africa's best known sounds. He is among the most famous voices to come out of West Africa.
know: He led the Étoile de Dakar and then the Super Étoile de Dakar, the bands that defined mbalax.
His album Egypt won the Grammy for Best Contemporary World Music Album in 2005.
He served as Senegal's Minister of Culture and Tourism from 2012 to 2013.

influenced.why: He sang the closing Wolof passage on Gabriel's In Your Eyes and toured with him in the late 1980s.

cousins.why: A national voice who turned a local rhythm into a global one.
Commanding singer at the front of a hard-driving dance band.

summary: Malian singer known as the Golden Voice of Africa, who came up in the Rail Band and Les Ambassadeurs before a solo career that mixed Mande griot singing with funk, jazz and synthesizers.
know: He is a descendant of Sundiata Keita, founder of the Mali Empire.
His breakthrough solo album Soro (1987) was recorded in Paris and set Mande melodies to modern production.
Amen (1991) was produced by Joe Zawinul and featured Wayne Shorter and Carlos Santana.

influencedBy.why: Weather Report keyboardist Joe Zawinul produced Amen and shaped its jazz-fusion sheen.
Carlos Santana played on Amen, adding Latin-rock guitar to his sound.

cousins.why: A huge, soaring voice that carries sacred intensity.
A singer whose voice alone can hold a whole song.

summary: Malian guitarist and singer whose hypnotic, modal playing drew a direct line between West African music and American blues. His records with Ry Cooder and Toumani Diabaté won Grammy Awards.
know: Talking Timbuktu, made with Ry Cooder, won the Grammy for Best World Music Album in 1995.
In the Heart of the Moon, with kora player Toumani Diabaté, won the same award in 2006.
He became mayor of his hometown Niafunké in 2004 and spent much of his time farming there.

influencedBy.why: He said hearing Hooker convinced him the blues had African roots, and his drones are often compared to Hooker's.

influenced.why: His international success opened the door for Saharan guitar bands, and Tinariwen's sound follows his modal blues.

cousins.why: Spare, rolling acoustic blues full of space.
Hill country blues built on repeating hypnotic riffs.

summary: Tuareg collective founded by Ibrahim Ag Alhabib whose rolling electric guitars and call-and-response vocals brought Saharan music to rock audiences. Their success sparked a wave of desert guitar bands.
know: Ibrahim Ag Alhabib built his first guitar as a boy from a tin can, a stick and bicycle wire.
Their international debut, The Radio Tisdas Sessions, came out in 2001 after the band played the first Festival au Désert.
Tassili, recorded acoustically in the Algerian desert with guests from TV on the Radio and Wilco's Nels Cline, won the 2012 Grammy for Best World Music Album.

influencedBy.why: Touré's modal Malian blues set the template for electric Saharan guitar that Tinariwen built on.

cousins.why: Droning, hypnotic guitar blues that locks into one groove.
Trance-like boogie built on a single riff.
Long, rolling guitar music made for driving across open space.

summary: Vibraphonist, percussionist and arranger known as the father of Ethio-jazz, who joined Ethiopian scales to jazz and Latin rhythms. His records found a new global audience through the Éthiopiques series and film soundtracks.
know: He was the first African student at Berklee College of Music.
He arranged and played with Duke Ellington's orchestra during Ellington's 1973 visit to Ethiopia.
Jim Jarmusch built the soundtrack of Broken Flowers (2005) around his music.

influencedBy.why: He studied Ellington's orchestration and later worked with his band in Addis Ababa.
His New York years in the Latin jazz scene led to the mambo and boogaloo feel of Afro-Latin Soul.
Modal jazz showed him how to set long improvisations over Ethiopian scales.

influenced.why: Nas and Damian Marley built As We Enter on a sample of Yègèllé Tezeta.
His tune is the backbone of As We Enter from Distant Relatives.

cousins.why: Jazz bandleader who reached for sounds and scales far outside the standard.
Bold Latin jazz with adventurous harmony.
Jazz that leans hard into groove and texture.

summary: Beninese singer and songwriter who mixes West African rhythms with funk, jazz and pop. She is one of the most decorated African artists at the Grammy Awards.
know: She moved to Paris in 1983, where she studied jazz and launched her international career.
Her 2018 album Remain in Light reworked the whole Talking Heads record with African arrangements.
She has won five Grammy Awards and is a long-serving UNICEF Goodwill Ambassador.

influencedBy.why: She has called Makeba her role model, the African woman who first showed her a global career was possible.
Brown's funk records were a teenage obsession and shape her rhythm sections.
She remade Remain in Light song by song, tracing its African roots.
She paid tribute with the 2019 album Celia, honoring Cruz's Afro-Cuban music.
Afrobeat's horn-driven grooves run through her funkiest work.
Franklin's soul singing was a key model for her vocal power.

cousins.why: A powerhouse voice fronting heavy funk.
A singer who became the voice of a whole continent.

summary: Nigerian singer from Surulere, Lagos, who became one of the faces of the global Afrobeats boom. His Made in Lagos album and the hit Essence pushed Nigerian pop into the US mainstream.
know: He broke through on Banky W's label Empire Mates Entertainment with Holla at Your Boy in 2010.
He sang on Drake's One Dance, which topped the Billboard Hot 100 in 2016.
The Essence remix with Justin Bieber reached the Hot 100 top 10, a first for a Nigerian song.

influencedBy.why: He has named Fela as a hero, and Afrobeat's groove sits under his mid-tempo style.
He often cites Marley, and reggae's easy sway runs through his records.

influenced.why: His work on One Dance helped turn Drake toward Afrobeats rhythms.
Essence, built around their duet, made Tems a global name.
His smooth Afropop crossover laid the path that Rema's generation followed.

cousins.why: The biggest star of a non-English pop wave that conquered US charts.
Island dance music that crossed over without losing its accent.

summary: Atlanta-born, Lagos-raised singer and producer whose upbeat party hits made him one of Nigeria's biggest stars. His song Fall became one of the longest-charting Nigerian songs in the US.
know: His breakout single Dami Duro came out in 2011, and he produced much of his early work himself.
Fall (2017) was certified gold in the United States.
His album Timeless (2023) earned him multiple Grammy nominations.

influencedBy.why: Fela's Afrobeat is the foundation of the Nigerian pop he grew up with.

cousins.why: The party-starting voice of a dance-pop movement that went global.
Feel-good dancehall pop built for clubs and radio.

summary: Nigerian singer, songwriter and producer with a low, smoky voice who became a major figure in global R&B after Wizkid's Essence. She has written and sung on Grammy-winning and Oscar-nominated songs.
know: She taught herself to produce and released her first single, Mr Rebel, in 2018.
Future's Wait for U, built on her song Higher and featuring her vocals, won a Grammy in 2023.
Love Me JeJe won the Grammy for Best African Music Performance in 2025.

influencedBy.why: She has named Hill as a key influence on her mix of singing, writing and conviction.
Their duet Essence launched her internationally.
Her unhurried, jazzy phrasing follows the neo-soul path Badu opened.

influenced.why: Wait for U was built around her song Higher and her voice.

cousins.why: Moody, conversational modern R&B.
A warm, understated voice over spare soul production.

summary: Nigerian singer who calls his sound Afrorave, mixing Afrobeats with trap and Indian and Arabic melodic touches. His song Calm Down became one of the biggest African hits ever.
know: He signed to Don Jazzy's Mavin Records in 2019, and his song Iron Man appeared on Barack Obama's summer playlist that year.
The Calm Down remix with Selena Gomez reached No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100.
Calm Down became the first song by an African artist to pass one billion streams on Spotify.

influencedBy.why: Wizkid's smooth crossover Afropop was the model his generation of Nigerian singers grew up on.

cousins.why: Melodic, effects-heavy rap built for big rooms.
A genre-blending young star who made his local scene global.

summary: South African singer who blends amapiano's log drums with R&B and pop. Her single Water made her a global star in 2023.
know: Water won the first Grammy for Best African Music Performance in 2024.
Water made her the first South African solo artist on the Billboard Hot 100 since Hugh Masekela in the 1960s.
She calls her sound popiano, a mix of pop and amapiano.

influencedBy.why: She has named Rihanna as a model for blending island roots with global pop.
She often cites Aaliyah, and her airy R&B vocals follow that style.
She has named Jackson as a reason she wanted to perform.
Amapiano's log-drum sound, which Kabza De Small helped define, is the base of her records.

cousins.why: Dance-forward R&B pop led by choreography and groove.
Silky R&B that mixes in rhythms from home.

summary: South African DJ and producer widely called the King of Amapiano, whose huge output helped turn the Pretoria and Johannesburg township sound into a continental movement.
know: He formed the duo Scorpion Kings with DJ Maphorisa.
His 2020 album I Am the King of Amapiano: Sweet & Dust set streaming records in South Africa.
Sponono, with DJ Maphorisa, brought Wizkid and Burna Boy onto an amapiano track.
keyAlbums: I Am the King of Amapiano: Sweet & Dust
Rumble in the Jungle (Scorpion Kings with Tresor)

influencedBy.why: South African deep house, led by Black Coffee, is the sound amapiano grew out of.

influenced.why: The amapiano sound he helped define is the base of her pop.
He produced Sponono with DJ Maphorisa, putting Burna Boy over amapiano drums.
Sponono also brought Wizkid into the amapiano sound.

cousins.why: Warm, patient house music made for long DJ sets.
A producer with a signature swing that crossed into pop.

summary: South African DJ and producer who took Afro house from Durban to the world's biggest clubs. His album Subconsciously won a Grammy.
know: Subconsciously won the Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Album in 2022.
He held a long-running weekly residency in Ibiza.
He co-produced Get It Together on Drake's More Life and worked on Drake's Honestly, Nevermind.

influencedBy.why: Chicago house set the soulful, steady template for his DJ style.
Heard's deep, melodic house is the direct ancestor of his sound.

influenced.why: He co-produced Get It Together and helped shape Drake's turn to house on Honestly, Nevermind.
His success made South African house the launch pad for amapiano producers.

cousins.why: Warm, organic electronic music that travels well.
A DJ who brought deep house to a global pop audience.

summary: Trio of Seo Taiji, Yang Hyun-suk and Lee Juno whose rap, dance and rock hybrid broke the ballad-heavy mold of Korean pop. They are widely credited as the starting point of modern K-pop.
know: They debuted on a TV talent show in 1992, got the lowest score from the judges, and their song Nan Arayo then topped the charts for weeks.
Seo Taiji had played bass in the heavy metal band Sinawe before forming the group.
Member Yang Hyun-suk went on to found YG Entertainment, home of Big Bang and Blackpink.

influencedBy.why: Their debut leaned on the new jack swing beats Riley pioneered.
Come Back Home borrowed the heavy, hazy West Coast rap sound of Cypress Hill.
Seo Taiji's metal background shows in the hard guitars of their later albums.

influenced.why: Yang Hyun-suk built YG Entertainment, and Big Bang, on the hip-hop idol model the trio created.
Blackpink came out of YG, the company founded by member Yang Hyun-suk.
Psy signed to YG and grew out of the Korean rap-pop scene the trio started.
BTS covered Come Back Home in 2017 and performed with Seo Taiji at his 25th anniversary concert.

cousins.why: Rap that freely mixed in rock guitars and attitude.
A group that set the template for an entire wave of pop acts.

summary: YG Entertainment boy group led by G-Dragon, who wrote and produced much of their music. Their hip-hop and electronic hits made them one of the most influential K-pop acts of their era.
know: Their 2007 single Lies, co-written by G-Dragon, was their breakthrough hit in Korea.
Fantastic Baby (2012) became one of the best known K-pop songs outside Asia.
Bang Bang Bang won Song of the Year at the 2015 Mnet Asian Music Awards.

influencedBy.why: Their label boss Yang Hyun-suk came from Seo Taiji and Boys and modeled the group on that hip-hop idol idea.
G-Dragon has cited Pharrell Williams, and the Neptunes' bright, minimal beats show up in their work.
Their mix of rap swagger and electronic pop follows the late 2000s Kanye sound.

influenced.why: Blackpink were built by the same YG team as a female counterpart to Big Bang.

cousins.why: A boy band that took creative control of its own songs.
The defining boy band of an earlier pop generation.

summary: South Korean rapper, singer and producer known for comic, high-energy dance songs. Gangnam Style made him the first viral global K-pop star.
know: Gangnam Style was the first YouTube video to reach one billion views, in December 2012.
He studied in the United States at Boston University and Berklee College of Music.
He signed with YG Entertainment in 2010, two years before Gangnam Style.

influencedBy.why: He has said seeing a Queen concert video made him want to be a performer.
He came up in the Korean rap-dance scene the trio launched.

cousins.why: Pop built on humor and over-the-top videos.
A viral novelty hit that turned into a real career.

summary: Seven-member group from Big Hit Entertainment that started as a hip-hop crew and became the best-selling act in K-pop history. They took Korean pop to the top of the US charts.
know: Love Yourself: Tear (2018) was the first K-pop album to reach No. 1 on the Billboard 200.
Dynamite (2020) was the first Billboard Hot 100 No. 1 by a South Korean act.
Leader RM spoke at the United Nations General Assembly in 2018.

influencedBy.why: They covered Come Back Home and performed with Seo Taiji, calling him a founding figure.
RM has named Nas as one of the rappers who got him into hip-hop.
RM and Suga have cited Eminem as a formative rap influence.

cousins.why: The biggest boy band of the same decade, with a huge fan base.
A vocal group that defined pop for its era.

summary: YG Entertainment girl group of Jisoo, Jennie, Rosé and Lisa, whose loud, drop-heavy singles made them the most popular K-pop girl group worldwide.
know: Most of their hits were produced by YG's in-house producer Teddy Park.
They were the first K-pop girl group to play Coachella, in 2019, and they headlined it in 2023.
Born Pink (2022) was the first album by a female K-pop group to top the Billboard 200.

influencedBy.why: They were built by the YG team behind Big Bang and share that hip-hop-meets-EDM approach.
Their label YG was founded by Seo Taiji and Boys member Yang Hyun-suk.

cousins.why: A girl group with distinct personalities that went global.
A vocal group that defined pop for its decade.

summary: Five-member group created by Min Hee-jin at ADOR whose soft vocals and breakbeat, Jersey club and late 1990s R&B touches moved K-pop away from loud maximalism.
know: Their debut single Attention and the song Hype Boy came out together in 2022 with no pre-release teasers.
Super Shy and ETA used fast Jersey club drum patterns, produced with 250 and others.
Their EP Get Up reached No. 1 on the Billboard 200 in 2023.

influencedBy.why: Their breezy late 1990s girl group R&B feel follows TLC and their peers.
The smooth group harmonies and R&B swing recall 1990s acts like SWV.

cousins.why: Light, breathy vocals over fast breakbeats and garage drums.
Cool, understated R&B singing over inventive beats.

summary: Composer, pianist and producer who co-founded Yellow Magic Orchestra and went on to an Oscar-winning film career and decades of ambient and experimental work.
know: He co-founded Yellow Magic Orchestra with Haruomi Hosono and Yukihiro Takahashi in 1978.
He shared the Academy Award for Best Original Score for The Last Emperor.
His 1980 track Riot in Lagos is often cited as an early blueprint for electro.

influencedBy.why: Hosono invited him into YMO and was his main creative partner in the band.
Kraftwerk's machine pop was a direct model for YMO and his early synth records.
Eno's ambient approach is a clear ancestor of his later minimal work.

influenced.why: He was a founding member, keyboardist and songwriter.
Riot in Lagos and YMO's music fed into the electro sound Bambaataa built on.
Jackson recorded a version of Sakamoto's YMO song Behind the Mask during the Thriller sessions.

cousins.why: Synthesizer music that moved easily between pop and film.
Electronic music that moves between beats and quiet ambient pieces.

summary: Band of Haruomi Hosono, Eiichi Ohtaki, Shigeru Suzuki and Takashi Matsumoto that proved rock could be sung in Japanese. Its members went on to shape city pop, YMO and decades of Japanese pop.
know: Their choice to sing rock in Japanese, not English, set off a famous debate in the Japanese music press.
Kaze o Atsumete was used in the 2003 film Lost in Translation.
Their final album was recorded in Los Angeles with Van Dyke Parks producing.
songs: Juuni Gatsu no Ame no Hi

influencedBy.why: Their guitar-led folk rock was openly modeled on Buffalo Springfield.
The jangling folk rock of The Byrds shaped their early sound.
Their rootsy, ensemble feel shows a debt to The Band.

influenced.why: Eiichi Ohtaki signed Yamashita's band Sugar Babe to his Niagara label and produced their debut.
The band was where Hosono first developed as a songwriter and bassist.
Hosono carried what he learned in the band into YMO.

cousins.why: Harmony-rich folk rock made by future stars.
A short-lived band whose influence grew huge after it ended.

summary: Singer, guitarist and producer who became the defining voice of Japanese city pop, known for lush harmonies and tight funk grooves. His records found a big new overseas audience online in the 2010s.
know: He started in the band Sugar Babe, whose debut was produced by Eiichi Ohtaki of Happy End.
Christmas Eve (1983) has returned to the Japanese charts nearly every winter for decades.
He produced and arranged his wife Mariya Takeuchi's records, including Plastic Love.

influencedBy.why: He has said the Beach Boys' harmonies shaped his vocal arranging, and Big Wave covers their songs.
He adored Spector's dense wall of sound records.
The blue-eyed soul of The Young Rascals is a stated favorite.
Ohtaki of Happy End gave him his start by producing Sugar Babe.
His funk guitar and smooth soul arrangements draw on Mayfield's records.

cousins.why: Glossy, jazzy studio pop with session-player precision.
Smooth, harmony-driven soft rock with funk underneath.
Bright horns, tight grooves and big vocal blends.

summary: Bassist, songwriter and producer who played in Happy End, made a run of exotica-flavored solo records, and then founded Yellow Magic Orchestra. He is one of the central figures in Japanese pop.
know: He was the bassist and a main songwriter in Happy End.
His mid 1970s albums Tropical Dandy and Bon Voyage co. mixed exotica, Okinawan music and New Orleans rhythm.
He formed YMO in 1978 after inviting Ryuichi Sakamoto and Yukihiro Takahashi to work on a cover of Martin Denny's Firecracker.

influencedBy.why: Buffalo Springfield was the template for his early folk rock with Happy End.
Hosono House's loose, homemade sound follows The Band.
Little Feat's New Orleans-flavored grooves fed into his Tropical Dandy period.
Kraftwerk showed him how pop could be built from machines, leading to YMO.

influenced.why: He founded the group and wrote much of its music.
He brought Sakamoto into YMO and was his key early collaborator.

cousins.why: A restless studio musician who moved from rock to electronic and ambient.
A pop craftsman and producer who kept switching styles.

summary: Band led by drummer, pianist and composer Yoshiki that mixed speed metal with classical piano and huge ballads. They are credited as founders of the visual kei movement.
know: Yoshiki and singer Toshi formed the band as childhood friends in Tateyama, Chiba.
Blue Blood (1989) made them stars, and Jealousy (1991) topped the Oricon chart.
Art of Life (1993) is a single song nearly half an hour long.

influencedBy.why: Yoshiki has said seeing Kiss made him want to play rock, and their makeup and staging fed visual kei.
Their galloping twin-guitar speed metal follows the British metal of Iron Maiden.
Judas Priest's high-pitched, fast metal is a clear ancestor of their sound.
Their mix of rock and grand, operatic ballads echoes Queen.

influenced.why: They set the template for Japanese metal acts that pair speed with spectacle.

cousins.why: Long, technically dazzling metal with classical ambition.
Big hooks, power ballads and arena-sized metal.

summary: Osaka band led by Yamantaka Eye that went from chaotic noise rock to long, drum-heavy psychedelic trance pieces. They became a cult touchstone for American indie and experimental bands.
know: They toured with Sonic Youth and Nirvana and played Lollapalooza in 1994.
Super Ae and Vision Creation Newsun traded noise for huge, looping rhythmic builds.
On July 7, 2007, they staged 77 Boadrum in Brooklyn with 77 drummers playing together.

influencedBy.why: Their early cut-up, absurd noise rock owes a lot to the Butthole Surfers.
Their long, locked-in trance rhythms follow Can's approach.
The driving, repeating pulse of their late 1990s work recalls Neu!

influenced.why: Animal Collective's tribal, looping psychedelia is often traced to Boredoms.

cousins.why: Heavy, noisy and unpredictable underground rock.
Cosmic, ritual-like music with a huge drum section.

summary: Singer, songwriter and producer raised between Tokyo and New York whose R&B-inflected debut became the best-selling album in Japanese history. She writes and produces her own music.
know: Her debut album First Love (1999) sold more than seven million copies in Japan.
She wrote and sang Simple and Clean and Hikari for the Kingdom Hearts video games.
Her mother was the famous enka singer Keiko Fuji.

influencedBy.why: Her debut brought the late 1990s US R&B sound of singers like Blige into J-pop.
The crisp, syncopated R&B production of the late 1990s shaped Automatic.

cousins.why: Cool, understated R&B singing over inventive production.
A pop artist who took control of her own sound and grew more adventurous.

summary: Group that fuses Japanese idol pop vocals and choreography with heavy metal backing. They became one of the most successful Japanese acts abroad.
know: They started as a sub-unit of the idol group Sakura Gakuin.
Metal Resistance (2016) reached No. 39 on the Billboard 200, the best showing by a Japanese act in decades.
They opened shows for Lady Gaga, Metallica and Red Hot Chili Peppers.

influencedBy.why: Their mix of speed metal and Japanese spectacle follows the path X Japan opened.
Their backing band's thrash riffs are rooted in Metallica-style metal.

cousins.why: Modern metal that happily mixes in pop and electronic sounds.
A gleeful collision of cute pop and heavy noise.

summary: Duo of producer Ayase and singer Ikura who turn short stories into fast, intricate pop songs. Their anime theme Idol became a global chart hit.
know: Each of their early songs adapted a short story posted on the writing site Monogatary.com.
Ayase started out as a Vocaloid producer before forming the duo.
Idol, the theme for Oshi no Ko, topped the Billboard Global Excl. US chart in 2023, a first for a Japanese song.

cousins.why: Anime-inspired electronic pop full of bright, emotional melodies.
Exact, melody-packed pop that rewards repeat listening.

summary: Composer known as Pancham who brought rock, funk, Latin and disco sounds into Hindi film music in the 1960s and 1970s. His scores remain among the most sampled and loved in Bollywood.
know: He was the son of the composer S.D. Burman and worked as his father's assistant before scoring on his own.
He was known for found sounds, such as blowing across bottles and rubbing comb and paper, in his arrangements.
He married singer Asha Bhosle, who sang many of his biggest songs, in 1980.

influencedBy.why: Latin big band rhythms like Prado's mambo show up all over his 1960s scores.
Western rock and roll fed the guitar-driven songs of Teesri Manzil.

influenced.why: His cabaret, rock and disco songs defined her 1970s sound.
He gave Rafi the youthful rock and roll songs of Teesri Manzil.
Rahman has cited Burman's genre-mixing as a model for his own film work.

cousins.why: A composer with sophisticated, instantly hummable arrangements.
A genre-crossing arranger with an ear for groove.
Bright, Latin-tinged pop orchestration.

summary: Playback singer known as the Nightingale of India whose voice defined Hindi film song for more than half a century. She recorded in dozens of Indian languages.
know: Her breakthrough came with Aayega Aanewala from the 1949 film Mahal.
She received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honor, in 2001.
She was the elder sister of singer Asha Bhosle.

influenced.why: Her elder sister's dominance pushed Asha to carve out a different, more playful style.
She sang for Rahman's scores, and her standard shaped the voices he wrote for.

cousins.why: A pure, flawless voice that defined a whole songbook.
A singer whose voice became the sound of a genre.

summary: Playback singer with a huge range who sang everything from ghazals to cabaret and disco in Hindi film. She is one of the most recorded singers in history.
know: Guinness World Records recognized her in 2011 as the most recorded artist in music history.
Her partnership with R.D. Burman produced many of the boldest Bollywood songs of the 1970s.
Cornershop's 1997 hit Brimful of Asha is a tribute to her.
keyAlbums: You've Stolen My Heart (with Kronos Quartet)

influencedBy.why: Her elder sister was the standard she measured herself against and moved away from.
Burman, later her husband, wrote the songs that defined her most adventurous period.

cousins.why: A singer who could move easily between jazz, blues and pop.
Cool, playful phrasing across many styles.

summary: Playback singer whose warm, flexible voice could handle romantic songs, devotional pieces and rock and roll numbers alike. He is one of the most loved voices in Indian film.
know: He adjusted his voice to suit each leading actor he sang for.
He won six Filmfare Awards for best male playback singer.
He won a National Film Award for Kya Hua Tera Wada in 1977.
songs: Aaja Aaja Main Hoon Pyar Tera

cousins.why: A smooth, warm voice that made romantic songs sound easy.
The defining male singer of a nation's popular song.

summary: Composer and producer who modernized Indian film music with digital production, world rhythms and Sufi devotion. He won two Academy Awards for Slumdog Millionaire.
know: He played keyboards for Ilaiyaraaja's orchestra before his first film score, Roja, in 1992.
He won Oscars for Best Original Score and Best Original Song (Jai Ho) for Slumdog Millionaire.
He wrote the music for Andrew Lloyd Webber's stage musical Bombay Dreams.

influencedBy.why: He worked as a keyboardist in Ilaiyaraaja's orchestra early in his career.
Burman's free mixing of Western and Indian styles was a key model.
He collaborated with Nusrat, whose qawwali shaped Rahman's Sufi songs.

influenced.why: They remade his Jai Ho as an English-language hit in 2009.

cousins.why: Synth-heavy film scores with big emotional themes.
A producer and composer equally at home in film and pop.

summary: Prolific composer who blended Tamil folk music with Western classical orchestration and pop, transforming South Indian film music from the late 1970s on.
know: His first film score was for Annakili in 1976.
He has composed music for well over a thousand films in several Indian languages.
His album How to Name It? (1986) set Western classical forms against Indian ragas.

influenced.why: Rahman played keyboards in his orchestra and learned film scoring there.

cousins.why: Folk music reshaped with classical structure and counterpoint.
A composer of lush, intricate arrangements for popular song.

summary: Pakistani singer who led his family's qawwali party and became the best known voice of Sufi devotional music worldwide. His collaborations brought qawwali into rock, film and electronic music.
know: He took over leadership of his family's qawwali group after his father's death and released many records with them.
Peter Gabriel signed him to the Real World label and used his voice on the Last Temptation of Christ soundtrack.
He sang with Eddie Vedder on two songs for the Dead Man Walking soundtrack in 1995.

influenced.why: Massive Attack remixed Mustt Mustt into a club hit in 1990.
Gabriel featured him on Passion, his Last Temptation of Christ score, and signed him to Real World.
Eddie Vedder sang with him on the Dead Man Walking soundtrack.
Buckley called him a hero, studied his singing, and interviewed him for a magazine.
His qawwali shaped Rahman's Sufi film songs, and the two worked together.

cousins.why: Devotional singing of overwhelming power.
Spiritual music that builds through long, ecstatic improvisation.
A sacred-trained voice that could lift a room.

summary: Egyptian singer known as the Star of the East, regarded as the greatest voice in twentieth century Arabic music. Her long concert performances drew listeners across the Arab world.
know: Her monthly Thursday night concerts were broadcast live on radio across the Arab world.
A single song in concert could last over an hour as she repeated and varied lines for the audience.
Enta Omri (1964) was her first song with composer Mohammed Abdel Wahab.

influenced.why: Robert Plant has often named her as a singer who changed his idea of what a voice could do.
She set the standard for Arabic singing that Fairuz's generation grew up on.
Her music was the classical Arabic backdrop for the raï singers of Algeria.
Taha drew on classical Arabic singing like hers in his rock fusion.

cousins.why: A voice that could stretch a single line into deep feeling.
A singer who became the voice of a whole region.

summary: Lebanese singer whose clear, gentle voice became one of the most beloved in the Arab world. Her work with the Rahbani brothers, and later her son Ziad, shaped modern Lebanese song.
know: Most of her classic songs were written by the Rahbani brothers, Assi and Mansour; she married Assi.
Her son Ziad Rahbani brought jazz harmony and funk into her music from the late 1970s.
Li Beirut sets new lyrics to the slow movement of Rodrigo's Concierto de Aranjuez.

influencedBy.why: She came up in a world shaped by Umm Kulthum, while choosing a shorter, lighter style of song.

cousins.why: A pure, clear voice tied to a people's sense of itself.
A singer who became a national symbol.

summary: Algerian singer known as the King of Raï who modernized the Oran folk style with synths, drum machines and funk. His 1992 hit Didi made raï an international sound.
know: He started recording as a teenager in Oran, then known as Cheb Khaled.
Didi (1992) became a hit across the Middle East, Europe and India.
Aïcha (1996), written by Jean-Jacques Goldman, topped the French charts.

influencedBy.why: Classical Arabic singing like hers is part of the vocal tradition he stretched over raï.

influenced.why: Khaled's international success with raï opened doors for Taha, and the two later shared the 1,2,3 Soleils concert.

cousins.why: A national rhythm turned into a world-touring pop sound.
A crowd-raising singer fronting a big dance band.

summary: Algerian-born singer who fused raï and chaabi with punk, rock and electronic music, first with the Lyon band Carte de Séjour and then solo. He was a leading voice of North African music in France.
know: He fronted Carte de Séjour, whose 1986 cover of Charles Trenet's Douce France became a statement for France's North African community.
Guitarist and producer Steve Hillage produced many of his solo records.
He recorded Rock el Casbah, an Arabic version of The Clash's song, and performed it with Mick Jones.

influencedBy.why: He loved The Clash's punk energy, covered Rock the Casbah, and played with Mick Jones.
Classical Arabic singing was part of the musical home he mixed with rock.
Khaled's modern raï was a key reference, and they performed together on 1,2,3 Soleils.

cousins.why: Punk energy mixed with immigrant and street music.
Punk spirit fused with a traditional music from home.

summary: Israeli singer from Tel Aviv's Hatikva Quarter who mixed traditional Yemenite Jewish songs with dance production. Her 1988 hit Im Nin'alu made her an international star.
know: She placed second at the 1983 Eurovision Song Contest with Hi.
Im Nin'alu, a setting of a 17th century Yemenite poem, topped the West German chart in 1988.
She sang on the 1992 re-recording of The Sisters of Mercy's Temple of Love.

influenced.why: Her vocals are the centerpiece of their 1992 version of Temple of Love.

cousins.why: Ancient-sounding melodies with a modern production.
A distinctive voice with an exotic, dramatic flair.

summary: Parisian singer known as the Little Sparrow whose raw, powerful voice made her the definitive voice of French chanson. Her songs remain worldwide standards.
know: Nightclub owner Louis Leplée discovered her singing on the street in 1935 and named her La Môme Piaf.
She wrote the lyrics of La Vie en rose.
She helped launch the careers of Yves Montand and Charles Aznavour.

influenced.why: She set the bar for dramatic, deeply felt chanson that Brel's generation followed.

cousins.why: A small woman with a voice full of lived experience.
A singer who gave a genre its most heartfelt standards.

summary: Belgian singer-songwriter whose intense, theatrical songs made him one of the greats of French chanson. English-speaking artists from Scott Walker to David Bowie spread his songs abroad.
know: He moved from Brussels to Paris in 1953, where producer Jacques Canetti gave him his start.
The revue Jacques Brel Is Alive and Well and Living in Paris opened off-Broadway in 1968.
His last album, Les Marquises (1977), was recorded after years away from music.

influencedBy.why: He came up in a Paris chanson world Piaf dominated, and his dramatic delivery follows hers.

influenced.why: Bowie sang Amsterdam and My Death in his early 1970s shows.
Simone recorded Ne me quitte pas in French.
Cohen admired Brel and shares his darkly poetic, sung-spoken style.
Stromae is often compared to Brel, a fellow Brussels singer, and has named him as an influence.

cousins.why: Literary, intense songs about love and mortality.
Theatrical songs full of sailors, drunks and dreamers.

summary: Singer, songwriter and provocateur who wrote for the biggest French pop singers and made bold concept albums. His records remain a major reference for indie and electronic musicians.
know: He wrote Poupée de cire, poupée de son, which won Eurovision in 1965 for France Gall.
Histoire de Melody Nelson (1971), arranged by Jean-Claude Vannier, is a cult classic of orchestral pop.
He recorded Aux armes et cætera in Kingston with Sly and Robbie in 1979.

influencedBy.why: Sly and Robbie backed him on Aux armes et cætera and led his reggae turn.

influenced.why: He wrote Comment te dire adieu for her.
Air's cool, string-laden French pop draws directly on Melody Nelson.
Beck's Paper Tiger borrows the Melody Nelson sound.
Portishead's dark, cinematic string arrangements echo his late 1960s records.

cousins.why: Spoken, cool vocals over striking arrangements.
A low, half-sung voice with a poet's ear.

summary: Parisian singer-songwriter whose wistful debut made her the face of the yé-yé era. She moved on to a long career of moody, sophisticated pop and remained a style icon for indie musicians.
know: Her 1962 debut single Tous les garçons et les filles sold millions and made her a star at 18.
She represented Monaco at the 1963 Eurovision Song Contest.
La Question (1971) was built around the guitar of Brazilian musician Tuca.

songs: Tous les garçons et les filles

influencedBy.why: Gainsbourg wrote Comment te dire adieu for her.
Like many yé-yé singers she started out under the spell of American rock and roll.

influenced.why: Damon Albarn recorded a duet with her in 1995, and Blur's gentler songs echo French pop of her era.
Air's soft, breathy French pop takes its mood from yé-yé singers like her.

cousins.why: A cool, understated voice singing gentle, melancholy pop.
Quiet, introspective songs carried by a soft voice and guitar.

summary: Belgian singer, rapper and producer who mixes house and hip-hop beats with the storytelling of French chanson. His songs have been hits across Europe and Africa.
know: Alors on danse topped charts across Europe in 2010.
His second album Racine carrée (2013) was one of the best-selling French-language albums of its decade.
He returned in 2022 with the album Multitude after a long break from music.

influencedBy.why: He has named Brel, a fellow Brussels singer, as an influence, and is often compared to him.
Kanye remixed Alors on danse, and Stromae's moody rap production follows the late 2000s Kanye sound.

cousins.why: Storytelling vocals over club-ready electronic beats.
Dance music with a sharp, self-aware songwriting voice.

summary: Duo of guitarist Michael Rother and drummer Klaus Dinger, both briefly in Kraftwerk, whose steady motorik beat became one of rock's most copied rhythms.
know: Rother and Dinger met while playing in an early lineup of Kraftwerk.
All three of their 1970s albums were produced by Conny Plank.
Dinger's relentless straight beat, later called motorik, is the band's signature.

influencedBy.why: Both members came out of an early Kraftwerk lineup.
Plank produced and engineered their records and shaped their sound.

influenced.why: Bowie has cited Neu! as a key influence on his late 1970s Berlin albums.
Eno championed them and worked with the closely linked Harmonia.
John Lydon has named Neu! as a favorite, and PiL's driving grooves show it.
Michael Rother co-founded Harmonia between Neu! albums.
Sonic Youth's long, driving guitar pieces show a debt to motorik rock.
LCD Soundsystem's steady, building songs use the motorik pulse.

cousins.why: Hypnotic, groove-locked German experimental rock.
Long, forward-rolling songs built on a steady beat.

summary: Experimental group set up with producer Uwe Nettelbeck who lived and recorded together in a converted schoolhouse in Wümme. Their collage of rock, noise and tape edits made them one of the most radical krautrock bands.
know: Polydor funded them with a studio in an old schoolhouse in Wümme, near Hamburg.
The Faust Tapes (1973) was sold in Britain by Virgin for the price of a single.
They recorded Outside the Dream Syndicate (1973) with minimalist violinist Tony Conrad.

influencedBy.why: Their droning repetition and noise owe a lot to the Velvet Underground.
Their sudden genre jumps and studio collage follow Zappa's early work.

influenced.why: Faust's noisy, open-ended experiments fed the art-noise rock Sonic Youth built on.

cousins.why: Wildly experimental rock that ignores the usual rules.
Noisy, collage-like psychedelic chaos.

summary: Supergroup of Michael Rother of Neu! and Dieter Moebius and Hans-Joachim Roedelius of Cluster, who made gentle, looping electronic rock in a farmhouse in rural Germany.
know: They lived and recorded together in the village of Forst in the Weserbergland.
Brian Eno called them the world's most important rock band and recorded with them in 1976.
Their sessions with Eno were finally released in 1997 as Tracks and Traces.

influencedBy.why: Michael Rother brought Neu!'s melodic guitar and pulse into the group.
Plank co-produced Deluxe.

influenced.why: Eno recorded with them and has said their music shaped his ambient direction.

cousins.why: Warm, hazy electronic music with a pastoral feel.
Patient, instrumental rock built from loops and texture.

summary: Producer and engineer whose studio near Cologne was the hub of German experimental music. He shaped key records by Kraftwerk, Neu!, Cluster and Harmonia and later worked with new wave bands across Europe.
know: He engineered and co-produced Kraftwerk's early albums, including Autobahn.
He produced all of Neu!'s 1970s albums and many records by Cluster.
His studio hosted Devo's debut sessions with Brian Eno and produced Eurythmics' first album, In the Garden.

influenced.why: Co-produced and engineered Autobahn and their early albums, helping shape their electronic sound.
Produced all three of their 1970s albums and helped build their spacious mix.
Co-produced Deluxe.
Eno recorded with Cluster at Plank's studio, work that fed his ambient era.
Devo recorded their debut, Q: Are We Not Men?, in his studio with Eno producing.

cousins.why: A producer whose studio space defined a whole scene's sound.
A studio experimenter who treated the console as an instrument.

summary: Group led by Florian Fricke that moved from early Moog synthesizer drones to spiritual piano and choir music. They are best known for their scores for Werner Herzog's films.
know: Their debut Affenstunde (1970) was one of the first German records built around the Moog synthesizer.
Fricke then gave up the Moog in favor of piano, guitar and voices.
They scored many Werner Herzog films, including Aguirre, the Wrath of God and Nosferatu.

influenced.why: Their sacred, chant-like atmospheres anticipate Dead Can Dance.

cousins.why: Patient, meditative music that shaped ambient.
Long, meditative German electronic soundscapes.

summary: Berlin band whose heavy, marching riffs, electronic layers and German vocals defined Neue Deutsche Härte. Their huge pyrotechnic live shows made them one of the biggest non-English rock acts.
know: All their lyrics are in German, sung by Till Lindemann.
Sehnsucht (1997) went platinum in the United States.
They covered Kraftwerk's Das Modell and Depeche Mode's Stripped.

influencedBy.why: They covered Das Modell and have cited Kraftwerk's cold German electronics.
They covered Stripped, and Depeche Mode's dark synth sound runs through their keyboards.
Ministry's industrial metal is a direct model for their riffs and drum machines.

cousins.why: Industrial rock with huge, machine-driven sound.
Theatrical, extremely heavy music built on spectacle.

summary: Reykjavík band fronted by Björk and Einar Örn that became the first Icelandic group to break internationally. Their quirky, angular pop launched Björk's career.
know: They grew out of the Reykjavík anarchist art collective Bad Taste (Smekkleysa).
Their 1987 single Birthday was named single of the week in the British music press and made them stars in Britain.
Their debut album Life's Too Good (1988) charted in Britain and the US.

influencedBy.why: Their wiry post-punk guitars and dramatic vocals draw on Siouxsie and the Banshees.
Their playful male and female vocal trade-offs echo The B-52's.

influenced.why: Björk came to the world as their singer before going solo.

cousins.why: Angular, unpredictable alternative rock with odd humor.
Off-kilter, playful alternative rock with a strong female voice.

summary: Icelandic composer and multi-instrumentalist who blends strings and piano with subtle electronic beats. He is a leading figure in modern neoclassical music.
know: He started out as a drummer in Icelandic hardcore and metal bands.
He won a BAFTA for his score to the TV series Broadchurch.
He also makes club-friendly electronic music in the duo Kiasmos with Janus Rasmussen.

influencedBy.why: He came up in the Icelandic scene Sigur Rós put on the map and shares their slow, glacial build.

cousins.why: Warm electronic music built around live instruments.
Slow-building instrumental music full of swelling emotion.

summary: Norwegian duo of Svein Berge and Torbjørn Brundtland whose warm, melodic electronica came out of the Bergen Wave scene. Their debut Melody A.M. became a defining chill-out record of the early 2000s.
know: Both members grew up in Tromsø before moving to Bergen.
Melody A.M. (2001) produced the hits Eple, Poor Leno and Remind Me.
They made the 2014 mini-album Do It Again with Robyn.

influencedBy.why: Their clean synth melodies follow Kraftwerk's electronic pop.
Their soft, vintage-synth downtempo shares Air's late 1990s sound.

cousins.why: Moody, slow electronic music made for late nights.
Gentle synth-pop with a melancholy streak.

summary: Swedish sibling duo of Karin Dreijer and Olof Dreijer whose eerie, pitch-shifted electronic pop grew more experimental with each album. Silent Shout is one of the most admired electronic records of the 2000s.
know: José González's acoustic cover of their song Heartbeats became famous through a 2005 Sony TV ad.
Silent Shout (2006) was named album of the year by Pitchfork.
They often appeared in masks and rarely gave interviews or played live early on.

influencedBy.why: Their dark, chilly synth-pop grows from the Depeche Mode tradition.
Björk's adventurous electronic pop is a clear ancestor of their sound.
Their cold, precise electronic textures follow Kraftwerk.

cousins.why: Daring electronic pop that bends voices and sounds.
Art-pop with unusual vocal processing and atmosphere.

summary: Group founded by uilleann piper Paddy Moloney that carried Irish traditional music to concert halls worldwide. Their many collaborations with rock and country stars made them Ireland's best known folk ambassadors.
know: Their music was used in Stanley Kubrick's film Barry Lyndon (1975).
In 1983 they were the first Western group to perform on the Great Wall of China.
They won six Grammy Awards, including for The Long Black Veil (1995), made with Mick Jagger, Sting and others.

influenced.why: They made Irish Heartbeat together, turning Morrison toward traditional Irish song.
Their success showed Irish traditional music could reach a big audience.
They helped revive interest in the traditional tunes the Pogues played at punk speed.

cousins.why: Traditional folk music played by a band with modern ears.
A virtuoso traditional player who collaborates across genres.

summary: Family band of the Brennan siblings and their Duggan uncles from County Donegal who moved from Irish-language folk to atmospheric, synth-washed Celtic pop. Their sound paved the way for Enya.
know: Theme from Harry's Game (1982) reached the UK top five, rare for a song sung in Irish.
Their album Legend, music for the TV series Robin of Sherwood, won a BAFTA.
Enya was a member from 1980 to 1982 before going solo.

influencedBy.why: The Chieftains proved Irish traditional music could travel, setting the stage for them.

influenced.why: Enya sang and played keyboards in the band before taking its layered sound solo.
Bono sang the duet In a Lifetime, and U2 used Harry's Game to close their shows.

cousins.why: A folk band that reshaped tradition with modern sounds.
Ethereal, ancient-sounding atmospheres.

summary: Dublin folk group of Ronnie Drew, Luke Kelly, Barney McKenna, Ciarán Bourke and later John Sheahan who made rough, spirited Irish ballad singing a popular force for fifty years.
know: They formed in 1962 playing sessions at O'Donoghue's in Dublin.
They charted in Britain several times in the 1960s, a rare feat for a traditional folk group.
Their 1987 single The Irish Rover with The Pogues reached the UK top ten.

influenced.why: The Pogues grew up on their records and recorded The Irish Rover with them.
Thin Lizzy's hit rock version of Whiskey in the Jar came from the ballad the Dubliners made popular.

cousins.why: A group that made traditional songs into popular sing-alongs.
A folk group that took old ballads to the charts.

summary: Irish singer and composer whose multi-tracked voice and keyboards created a lush, meditative sound. She is the best-selling Irish solo artist.
know: She works with producer Nicky Ryan and lyricist Roma Ryan, building songs from many layers of her own voice.
Orinoco Flow (1988) topped the UK singles chart.
May It Be, from The Lord of the Rings, was nominated for an Academy Award.

influencedBy.why: She sang and played keyboards in her family band before going solo with Nicky Ryan, their former manager.

cousins.why: Ethereal, layered voices floating over shimmering sound.
